designations.fra: Maximum capacity of partial weighing ranges

eng: Maximum capacity of partial weighing ranges

terms.designation: Maximum capacity of partial weighing ranges

definitions.content:
With the exception of the last partial weighing range, the requirements in Table 4 shall be complied with, according to the accuracy class of the instrument.
Table 4
ClassⅠⅡⅢⅣ
$\mathrm{Max}_{i}/e_{i+1}$≥50000≥5000≥500≥50
Example for a multi-interval instrument: Maximum capacity, Max = 2/5/15 kg, class III Verification scale interval, $ e=1/2/10\mathrm{g} $ This instrument has one Max and one weighing range from Min = 20 g to Max = 15 kg. The partial weighing ranges are: $$ \mathrm {M i n} = 2 0 \mathrm {g}, \mathrm {M a x} _ {1} = 2 \mathrm {k g}, e _ {1} = 1 \mathrm {g}, n _ {1} = 2 0 0 0 $$ $$ \mathrm {M i n} _ {2} = 2 \mathrm {k g}, \mathrm {M a x} _ {2} = 5 \mathrm {k g}, e _ {2} = 2 \mathrm {g}, n _ {2} = 2 5 0 0 $$ $$ \mathrm {M i n} _ {3} = 5 \mathrm {k g}, \mathrm {M a x} _ {3} = \mathrm {M a x} = 1 5 \mathrm {k g}, e _ {3} = 1 0 \mathrm {g}, n _ {3} = 1 5 0 0 $$ The maximum permissible errors on initial verification (mpe) (see 3.5.1) are: $$ \begin{array}{l} \mathrm {f o r} m = 0 \mathrm {g} \mathrm {t o} 5 0 0 \mathrm {g} \quad \mathrm {m p e} = \pm 0. 5 e _ {1} = \pm 0. 5 \mathrm {g} \\ \mathrm {f o r} m > 5 0 0 \mathrm {g} \mathrm {t o} 2 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \quad \mathrm {m p e} = \pm 1 e _ {1} = \pm 1 \mathrm {g} \\ \end{array} $$ $$ \mathrm {f o r} m > 2 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \mathrm {t o} 4 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \quad \mathrm {m p e} = \pm 1 e _ {2} \quad = \pm 2 \mathrm {g} $$ $$ \mathrm {f o r} m > 4 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \mathrm {t o} 5 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \quad \mathrm {m p e} = \pm 1. 5 e _ {2} \quad = \pm 3 \mathrm {g} $$ $$ \mathrm {f o r} m > 5 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \mathrm {t o} 1 5 0 0 0 \mathrm {g} \quad \mathrm {m p e} = \pm 1 e _ {3} \quad = \pm 1 0 \mathrm {g} $$ Whenever the variation of the indication due to certain influence factors is limited to a fraction or multiple of e, this means, in a multi-interval instrument, that e is to be taken according to the load applied; particularly at or near zero, load $ e=e_{1}. $
